A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WorldForge with the same authors, core modules, and principal benchmarks. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality, camera-trajectory, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–3, together with qualitative comparisons and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and adds quantitative component and backbone evaluations, runtime breakdowns, channel statistics, and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The depth-warping pipeline and IRR, FLF, and DSG mechanisms remain substantively the same. DSG's explicit magnitude-normalization factor is replaced by stated equal-length normalization. Newly documented guidance schedules and channel-selection settings clarify implementation; the PDFs do not establish a redesigned underlying method.

E1.justification: The principal static and dynamic generation tasks, LLFF, Tanks and Temples, MipNeRF 360, and diverse image/video coverage remain. v3 adds targeted fast-motion and heavy-occlusion scenarios in Supplementary Figure 7. Its explicit naming of DAVIS does not establish that this source was absent from v1's less specifically described video evaluation.

E2.justification: The principal 3D and 4D comparator sets remain unchanged. v3 additionally evaluates standard CFG as a direct alternative to DSG in main Table 3 and Supplementary Figure 1. ReCamMaster already participated in v1's qualitative and runtime comparisons; v3's explanation of its exclusion from quality/trajectory tables does not add or remove that baseline.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix B describes frame-wise Inception-V3 features for its simplified FVD; v3 Supplementary Sections 2.2–2.4 specify clip-level I3D features and change FVD resizing from 299 to 224 pixels. Reference construction changes from singleton augmentation to curated references and aggregated evaluation sets, and relative-pose definitions are revised. New LongCat, distilled, and super-resolution configurations extend evaluation. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing that retained scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation beyond v1's qualitative component, SVD, and depth-model ablations. It adds quantitative component ablations, standard-CFG and no-beta DSG tests, channel-filtering statistics, quantitative backbone comparisons including LongCat, Farneback-versus-RAFT tests, challenging-motion analyses, and illustrated failures. Supplementary Figure 5 also compares single-pass and iterative large-angle generation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run dispersion, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new channel-filtering frequencies are descriptive mechanism analyses, and additional evaluation sample counts do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The headline generation and trajectory values are retained, including WorldForge FID 96.08 and FVD 93.17. v3 adds substantial results: quantitative ablations, SVD/LongCat scores, LongCat throughput, component runtimes, channel statistics, and robustness findings. For example, the new CFG replacement obtains FID 120.91 and FVD 109.1. Existing runtimes are merely converted to frames/minute; revised metric descriptions prevent interpreting retained scores as same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: v3 Supplementary Section 2.3 revises relative-pose definitions to use consecutive pose transforms T_i^-1 T_(i+1), replacing v1 Appendix B.3's direct position differences and differently ordered rotation increments. This changes documented mathematical definitions. The diffusion/flow equivalence proof and core FLF mathematics remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v3's abstract adds the explicit claim of supporting 'over a dozen' downstream applications. The principal claims—training-free, model-agnostic 3D/4D control through three complementary modules and state-of-the-art quality—remain. Editing, stabilization, and try-on were already claimed and illustrated in v1, so this is a limited headline-claim expansion.

C2.justification: v3 replaces much of DSG's manifold-interpolation explanation with an orthogonal-guidance account motivated by large velocity-angle differences. It adds explanations of FLF robustness and why reference-based reconstruction metrics are unsuitable for imagined views. Severe-depth-error limitations are retained and illustrated, real-time infeasibility is newly acknowledged, and v1's explicit small-object/fine-detail control limitation is omitted.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies actionable defaults: 50 sampling steps, IRR during approximately the first 20, phased FLF channel limits, metric normalization constants, weights, DSG scale, and Farneback settings. It also documents editing with masks and an edited first frame, iterative clip chaining, evaluation reference counts, and component timing. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused positioning against RePaint, Xiao et al.'s prior motion-channel work, and APG's orthogonal guidance, clarifying how its components relate to existing techniques. It also adds references for LongCat, RAFT, and implementation tools. The broader positioning around training-free video priors and the three related-work categories remains intact.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten or condensed. Separate static and dynamic experiment sections are merged. Detailed FLF mathematics, demonstrations, efficiency discussion, and limitations are reorganized into a substantially expanded, separately structured supplement.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the single-column layout with two columns, rearranges the teaser, and merges the original static and dynamic comparison figures. Main benchmark tables are reorganized by task instead of metric family. Several existing demonstrations move to the supplement, while new ablation tables, a channel-frequency plot, robustness comparisons, and qualitative panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 clearly improves implementation disclosure and component validation through explicit settings, quantitative ablations, and robustness/failure examples. However, it changes the stated FVD feature extractor and reference-set construction while retaining identical headline scores, without explaining whether descriptions were corrected or results recomputed. This unresolved connection between protocols and results prevents confidently weighing the documentary and analytical gains against uncertainty in the quantitative evidence.
